priya.who: Priya, 34, marketing coordinator, not technical. Uses an iPhone 15 and a Windows 11 laptop at home.
priya.task: Move 200 to 500 photos and short videos from her iPhone to her Windows laptop about once a month, to edit and back them up.
priya.current_methods: Sends batches to herself on WhatsApp (which compresses them), or plugs in a USB cable and fights with the Windows Photos import.

marcus.who: Marcus, 27, sales rep, comfortable with apps but not a programmer. Uses a Samsung Galaxy phone and a MacBook Air.
marcus.task: Send screenshots, PDFs and phone videos between his phone and laptop several times a day.
marcus.current_methods: Telegram saved messages and Google Drive, because AirDrop does not work with Android.

elena.who: Elena, 41, freelance video editor. Uses a Mac Studio, a Windows workstation for rendering, and an iPhone.
elena.task: Move 20 to 200 GB project folders with thousands of files between the Mac and the Windows PC every week.
elena.network: Studio Wi-Fi and Ethernet on the same router.
elena.current_methods: Copies to an external SSD and walks it over, or uploads to WeTransfer overnight.

sam.who: Sam, 30, software developer who avoids cloud services for privacy. Uses an Ubuntu Linux laptop and an Android phone.
sam.task: Send documents, APKs and photos between phone and laptop a few times a week without any cloud account.
sam.current_methods: LocalSend, KDE Connect, or scp from a terminal.

grace.who: Grace, 45, office manager at a 10-person accounting firm. Staff use Windows PCs and company iPhones. An outside IT contractor manages the PCs.
grace.task: Get scanned contracts and phone photos of receipts from staff phones onto office PCs every day.
grace.network: Office Wi-Fi; visitors use a guest network.
grace.current_methods: Staff email attachments to themselves, which bounce when files are large.

kenji.who: Kenji, 20, university student. Uses an Android phone, a Windows laptop and an iPad.
kenji.task: Share lecture recordings, slides and notes between his own devices and with classmates sitting next to him.
kenji.network: Campus Wi-Fi, which usually blocks devices from seeing each other, and his phone hotspot.

linda.who: Linda, 66, retired teacher with low confidence in technology. Uses an iPad, an iPhone and an old Windows desktop.
linda.task: Copy videos of her grandchildren from her iPhone to the Windows desktop to keep them safe.
linda.network: Home Wi-Fi set up by her son.
linda.current_methods: Emailing videos to herself, which fails for anything long, then asking her son for help.

ravi.who: Ravi, 38, travel photographer. Uses an Android phone and a MacBook Pro.
ravi.task: Move 10 to 30 GB of RAW photos and drone videos from his phone to his laptop while travelling.
ravi.network: Hotel Wi-Fi that isolates guests, or no internet at all, so he uses his phone hotspot.
ravi.current_methods: USB-C cable with Android File Transfer, which often disconnects mid-copy.

platforms.label: Native apps on all five platforms
platforms.launch: Native apps for iPhone/iPad, Android, macOS, Windows and Linux from the usual app stores and website. Installers are about 10 MB.
platforms.current: Desktop apps for macOS and Windows (135 MB installers) and an Android app. iPhone and iPad only work through a web page that first requires installing a security certificate profile in iOS Settings.

signed.label: Signed, notarized installers
signed.launch: Installers are signed and notarized, so macOS and Windows open them without warnings.
signed.current: Installers are unsigned: macOS says it cannot check the app for malicious software and Windows shows "Windows protected your PC"; the user has to find the hidden way to open it anyway.

pairing.label: Tap a nearby device and compare a 6-digit code
pairing.launch: To connect two devices the first time, tap the other device in the Nearby list, then check that both screens show the same 6-digit number and press Accept on the other device.
pairing.current: To connect two devices, open "Pair a device" on the receiver, type its 30-character code on the sender (or paste a long invitation link), approve on the receiver, then press "Confirm connection" on the sender.

remembered.label: Devices stay paired after restarts
remembered.launch: Once connected, the two devices stay paired, including after closing the app or restarting; next time they just appear as ready.
remembered.current: A pairing is forgotten when either app closes and after 24 hours; the user pairs again each time.

two_way.label: One pairing works in both directions
two_way.launch: One pairing lets either device send to the other.
two_way.current: A pairing only works in one direction; to send back, the user pairs again from the other device.

auto_accept.label: Optional auto-accept from your own devices
auto_accept.launch: Files from your own paired devices can arrive automatically (a setting, on by default for devices you mark as yours); from anyone else you approve the file list first.
auto_accept.current: The receiver must review and approve every incoming file list, even from their own devices.

save_location.label: Files land in Downloads / Files / Photos
save_location.launch: Received files go straight to the Downloads folder on computers, the Files app on iPhone and the Downloads folder on Android, with a "Show in folder" button; photos and videos can be saved to the photo library in one tap.
save_location.current: Received files are kept in a hidden app data folder with a long random name; on phones each file has to be exported one at a time through a save dialog.

share_sheet.label: Send from the share sheet
share_sheet.launch: On phones, Drift appears in the Share menu of Photos, Files and other apps, and on computers files can be dropped on the window or tray icon.
share_sheet.current: Files can only be chosen from inside the Drift app with its own file picker.

background.label: Receives in the background on computers
background.launch: On computers Drift keeps running in the menu bar or system tray, so a computer can receive while its window is closed.
background.current: Drift only receives while its window is open.

qr_scan.label: Camera QR scanning
qr_scan.launch: If a device does not appear in the Nearby list, scan a QR code on the other screen with the phone camera.
qr_scan.current: If a device does not appear in the Nearby list, the user types an IP address, a port number and the 30-character code.

updates.label: Automatic updates
updates.launch: The app updates itself securely in the background.
updates.current: Each new version must be downloaded and installed by hand.

common.network: Works between devices on the same Wi-Fi network or phone hotspot. It does not send over the internet.
common.security: End-to-end encrypted, files are checked for corruption on arrival, and interrupted transfers resume.
common.speed: Usually several times faster than cloud upload and download because files go directly over the local network.
common.price: Free, with no account or sign-up.

internetFeature: If the devices are not on the same network, Drift sends through an encrypted relay over the internet instead, more slowly.

completes_first_transfer.instructions: Read `persona` and `product`. Using only the product exactly as described, would this person get through installing it on both devices, connecting them, and finishing their first transfer for `persona.task` on `persona.network`, without giving up and going back to `persona.current_methods`?

keeps_using.instructions: Read `persona` and `product`. Suppose this person did finish one transfer with the product exactly as described. One month later, would they still be choosing it for `persona.task`, instead of `persona.current_methods`?

pairing_method.instructions: Which way of connecting two devices for the first time would this person be most likely to complete correctly on the first try, without help?

criteria.tap_and_compare: Tap the other device in a Nearby list, check both screens show the same 6-digit number, and press Accept.
criteria.scan_qr: Point the phone camera at a QR code shown on the other screen.
criteria.type_short_code: Type a 6-digit code shown on the other screen.
criteria.paste_link: Copy a long invitation link on one device and paste it on the other.
criteria.type_long_code: Type a 30-character code plus an IP address and port.

receive_policy.instructions: Which rule for incoming files would this person want for files sent from their own devices?

criteria.auto_accept_own: Files from devices they have marked as their own arrive automatically; files from anyone else need approval.
criteria.ask_every_time: Show the file list and ask them to approve every transfer, even from their own devices.
criteria.accept_anyone: Accept files from any device on the network automatically.

save_location.instructions: Where would this person want files they receive from their own devices to be saved, so they can find and use them afterwards?

criteria.downloads: The normal Downloads folder (Files app on iPhone), with a button to show the file.
criteria.photo_library: Photos and videos in the phone or computer photo library; other files in Downloads.
criteria.ask_each_time: A save dialog asking where to put each transfer.
criteria.app_folder: A folder inside the app that they open from the app.

deal_breaker.instructions: If this person stopped using the current preview described in `current_preview`, which single problem would most likely be the reason?

criteria.install_warnings: Security warnings when installing on macOS or Windows.
criteria.no_iphone_app: No real iPhone/iPad app; the certificate-profile web page.
criteria.pairing_effort: Typing long codes and the approve-then-confirm steps.
criteria.repairing: Having to pair again after closing the app, and pairing separately for each direction.
criteria.hidden_files: Received files hidden in an app folder or exported one at a time.
criteria.network_blocked: Devices cannot see each other on their Wi-Fi.
criteria.no_internet_mode: Cannot send when the devices are on different networks.

needs_internet_often.instructions: For `persona.task`, would this person often need to send between devices that are not on the same Wi-Fi network or hotspot?

network_likely_blocks_lan.instructions: Is `persona.network` likely to stop two devices on it from discovering or connecting to each other directly?

expects_background_on_phone.instructions: Would this person expect a long transfer to keep going while their phone is locked or they switch to another app?

cares_about_install_size.instructions: Would a 135 MB installer instead of a 10 MB one noticeably reduce this person's willingness to install the app?
